params.body:
A bench for the second reader: classify@2's 80 frozen cases run through production's consensus code (`verifyBatch`, the comparison, the judge), and the labels consensus settles on scored against the expected answers beside Model A alone and Model B alone. It answers what Model B adds to Haiku 5.5 and what it breaks.

## What it shows

Two runs, Haiku 5.5 as Model A, three passes each:

| | Sonnet 5.5 as B (judge Opus 5.5) | Mistral Large 3 as B (judge Sonnet 5) |
|---|---|---|
| Band, A alone to consensus | 98% to 99% | 98% to 97% |
| POEM balanced | 100% to 100% | 100% to 99% |
| Unsupported cohort | 1% to 1% | 1% to 13% |
| Planted instructions resisted | 100% to 100% | 100% to 92% |
| Fixed per pass | 1.3 bands | 1 band |
| Broken per pass | 0.7 bands | 1.7 bands, 0.7 POEM, 8.7 cohorts, 0.3 planted |
| B disagreed with A | 27 of 73 cases | 52 of 71 cases |
| Disagreements on a case A got wrong | 7% | 4% |
| Cost per 1,000 signals, all three | $30.40 | $10.02 |

- **Mistral Large 3 as Model B breaks more than it fixes.** Its labels change the outcome only through the judge, and when the judge sides with B it takes B's labels whole, cohorts included. That is how Haiku's 1% unsupported cohorts become 13%: c53 got Gen Alpha in all three passes; c04, c07, c34, c39, c45 and c56 got cohorts in two. The one thing it fixed is the band on c45 (and c24 once).
- **Sonnet 5.5 as Model B is close to neutral**: it fixed the band on c45 and c04 and broke it on c73, at three times the cost.
- **As a flag on Haiku's mistakes, both catch all of them, but nearly every flag is noise**: Haiku got 2 cases wrong per pass, and Mistral disagreed on 52.
- **Into the gold set**: agreements were right on POEM and band every time with either B. With Mistral there are fewer (19 per pass against 47), and the judge's verdicts were right on 92%.

## How far this is from production

- **The judge sits on every batch here.** Production sits on about one batch in ten (`judge.sampleRate` 0.1) and only for routing differences; without a sitting, a disagreement is recorded and A's labels stay. So in production the label effect is roughly a tenth of the table above. With Mistral as B, that is still about one unsupported cohort per 100 signals that Haiku alone would not have given.
- **Model B gets no gold-set examples here.** The run uses a scratch database so the bench never writes to the real gold set; production gives B up to five.
- **The two runs differ in more than Model B.** The workbench run used Opus 5.5 as judge. The box run used production's saved configuration, whose `classify-judge` is Sonnet 5.
- **The suite was written against these cases.** The classify prompt's POEM rules and classify@2's labels were set on these cases, so Model A starts near the ceiling. A second reader has little room to fix anything, and any change it makes is more likely to break.

## enrich-verify is not covered

`verifyConceptMatches` vetoes the new concepts enrich proposes. Framing it on frozen cases would need a frozen set of concept proposals with an editor's reading of which ones should stand. classify@2's cases do not carry that, so this bench says nothing about enrich-verify.

## What changed in the code

- `packages/pipeline/consensus.mjs`: `verifyBatch`, `resolveDisagreements` and `resolveDisagreement` take an optional `trace` array and push the sitting, Model B's call and the judge's call into it. Production passes nothing, and behaves as before.
- `packages/bench/consensus.mjs`, `consensus-report.mjs`: run the suite, score each pass (labels per role, fixed and broken per measure, where each case ended, the flag, the gold set, cost) and render the report.
- `packages/bench/classify.mjs`: `aggregate` and `missesOf` are split out of `scorePass` for reuse. The classify report is byte-identical before and after.
- `bin/bench.mjs`: `--verify`, `--judge`, `--sitting always|production`. A consensus run sets its own scratch database and refuses `store/signals.db`. It also refuses a judge equal to Model B.
- `bench/suites/consensus/1/`: classify@2's cases and taxonomy, byte for byte (same digests), with no gates.
- `test/bench-consensus.test.mjs`: the real `verifyBatch` with Model B and the judge answering through a stand-in fetch.
- `bench/README.md`: a section on the suite and a changelog line. `bench/reports/consensus@1.md` holds both runs.

Full suite 1499 of 1505; the six failures are report-render, which needs pdftoppm on the machine that ran it.
params.title: consensus@1: a bench for the second reader
